alt: No 2023 model year was sold in the US; the redesigned Trax arrived for 2024.

issues.t: PCV valve and valve cover failure
issues.sym: Check engine light for a lean condition (often P0171), a whistle or hiss from the engine, rough idle, or oil leaks and oil burning.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation valve is built into the plastic valve cover. When it splits or sticks it causes a vacuum leak, and the usual fix is a new cover. GM tells technicians to test the PCV system before replacing the cover.
issues.next: Have a shop check for a vacuum leak at the valve cover and fix it before extra crankcase pressure pushes out other seals.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from housings and turbo lines
issues.sym: Sweet coolant smell, drips under the front, a low coolant message, losing heat in the cabin, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Plastic coolant outlet and thermostat housings, their gaskets and the turbo coolant connections on this engine are known to crack or seep as they age.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the leak traced and fixed soon. Stop driving if the temperature warning comes on.

issues.t: Turbo icing and power loss in cold weather
issues.sym: Sluggish acceleration or a sudden loss of power in very cold weather, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Moisture in the intake and crankcase vent system can freeze in the turbo plumbing. GM issued bulletins adding a PCV heater or updated charge air cooler and for checking the intake for ice.
issues.next: Ask a Chevrolet dealer whether the cold-weather bulletin update has been done on your car.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering assist
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often with a power steering warning on the dash.
issues.why: The steering column housing could wear against the power steering circuit board and cut the electric assist. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check the VIN for this recall. If the steering goes heavy, slow down, pull over safely and have the car inspected before driving on.

issues.sym: Usually no symptom. The airbag light may come on in some cases.
issues.why: A diagnostic routine in the airbag software could block the front airbags and seat belt pretensioners from firing in a crash. GM recalled the cars for a software fix, and some 2015-2016 cars needed a second recall because the first update was incomplete.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls and have the software updated as soon as possible.

issues.t: Seat belt and key reminder chimes silent
issues.sym: No chime when the driver is unbuckled or when the key is left in the ignition.
issues.why: Radio software could stop these warning chimes from sounding. GM recalled the cars to update the radio.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls and have the radio software updated.

issues.t: Front lower control arm weld can break
issues.sym: Clunking from the front, the car pulling or wandering, or uneven steering.
issues.why: A weld in the front lower control arm may not have been made properly. If it breaks, the arm can partly separate and the wheel can toe outward. GM ran two recalls covering different build ranges.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the front end clunks or the car pulls suddenly, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Multiple warning lights and intermittent no-start
issues.sym: Several warning lights come on at once, or the car sometimes won't crank or start.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for this combination of warning lights and intermittent no-crank on the Trax. Weak battery voltage or poor connections are a common starting point for diagnosis.
issues.next: Have the battery, cables and charging system tested, then have stored codes read by a shop.

issues.t: Airbag module left in factory mode
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may stay on.
issues.why: The airbag control module on some cars may have left the factory still in manufacturing mode, so the airbags might not deploy in a crash. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have it done right away.

issues.sym: Knocking or banging from the engine, a reduced engine power message, sudden loss of power or stalling. In the worst cases a connecting rod breaks through the block.
issues.why: Owners and a class action lawsuit report internal engine failures on GM's 1.2L three-cylinder turbo. GM has issued bulletins about engine noise on this engine.
issues.next: If the engine starts knocking or loses power, stop driving and have it towed to a dealer while it is under warranty.

issues.sym: The driver display blanks out, so speed and warning lights are not shown.
issues.why: Software in a vehicle control module could intermittently blank the instrument display. GM recalled affected cars for a software update.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check the VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank or distorted
issues.sym: The rear camera shows a blank, frozen or distorted picture when in Reverse.
issues.why: A fault can stop the rearview camera from showing a proper image. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and use mirrors and look back carefully until it is fixed.
